page.title: Content Marketing Operation Services Explained
page.description: Learn what content marketing operations cover, the seven workflow stages, tool stacks, timelines, roles and when to hire an external partner.
page.h1: What is included in content marketing operation services?
page.definition: Content marketing operation services are the end-to-end systems, workflows and governance that turn strategy into published assets on schedule and on brand. They cover intake, briefing, production, review, approval, publishing and reporting across articles, video, email and social, with named owners, tool stacks and measurable cycle times.
page.quick_answer: Map your current workflow to the seven standard stages, assign one owner per stage, choose tools for calendar, briefs, publishing and reporting, then set cycle-time targets. If gaps exceed internal capacity, scope an external partner for the missing workstreams.

sections.h2: What workflow stages does a content operation cover?

blocks.p: A complete content operation runs through seven stages, each with one owner and one output: intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting.

ul: Intake captures requests and prioritises against strategy
Brief defines audience, angle, format, SEO targets and deadline
Production creates draft assets — copy, design, video, audio
Review gathers stakeholder feedback in a single round
Approval records sign-off from brand, legal and product leads
Publishing pushes live to CMS, email, social and syndication
Reporting measures performance against KPIs and feeds back to intake

sections.h2: Which tools support each stage of the content pipeline?

blocks.p: Tool choices cluster around four functions: planning, briefing, publishing and reporting, with hand-off automation between them.

sections.h2: How long does a typical content cycle take from brief to publish?

blocks.p: A realistic cycle for a long-form article is five to ten working days from approved brief to publish, most of it in review.

ol: Day one to two: production writes and designs first draft
Day three to four: review consolidates stakeholder comments
Day five: approval records final sign-off
Day six to seven: publishing schedules and pushes live
Day eight onward: reporting captures early performance

sections.h2: What roles and approvals keep quality consistent?

blocks.p: Each stage needs a named owner; small teams combine roles but the approval gates stay distinct.

ul: Content strategist owns intake and brief quality
Writer, designer or video producer owns production output
Editor or subject expert owns review consolidation
Brand, legal and product leads own approval gates
Publishing specialist owns CMS deployment and scheduling
Analyst owns reporting dashboards and insight loop

sections.h2: When should you bring in an external partner for content operations?

blocks.p: Engage a partner when internal capacity cannot meet cycle-time targets, when tool stacks need architecture, or when a new content type requires specialised production.

ul: Cycle time exceeds ten working days for standard articles
Review rounds regularly exceed two per piece
Reporting lacks attribution to pipeline or revenue
New formats such as video series or podcasts need end-to-end workflow design

faq.q: How do content operations differ from content strategy?
faq.a: Strategy sets the why, who and what; operations build the how, when and who-does-what. Operations turn strategic themes into repeatable workflows, tool configs, approval gates and measurable cycle times so every piece ships on schedule.

faq.q: What is the minimum viable content operations stack for a small team?
faq.a: A shared calendar in Asana or Airtable, brief templates in Google Docs, publishing through WordPress or HubSpot, and a GA4 dashboard reviewed weekly. One person can own all stages if volume stays below four long-form pieces per month.

faq.q: How does West Peek Productions engage with content operations work?
faq.a: West Peek Productions scopes content operations work per engagement; it does not publish a fixed price. Send the scope for a quote. The team maps your seven stages, assigns owners, selects tools and sets cycle-time targets before building or fixing the workflow.

faq.q: What metrics prove a content operation is healthy?
faq.a: Track cycle time from approved brief to publish, revision rounds per piece, on-time publish rate and capacity utilisation across writers, designers and approvers. A healthy system shows declining cycle time, fewer than two revision rounds and ninety percent on-time rate.
